page: Amazon Web Services m6g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores built on the ARM64 Neoverse-N1 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system includes 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the m6g.4xlarge in the average tier for most multi-core and database operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score is 24287.64, and the Passmark database operations score reaches 10352.18. Redis SET operations perform at 18.83 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput is measured at 18.69 GB/sec. However, single-threaded performance is a notable tradeoff, with weak results in gzip compression at 20.29 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.63 GB/sec. Passmark memory performance and LLM inference processing speeds also rank in the weak to poor categories.

Utilizing custom ARM64 silicon allows this server to deliver resource density and power efficiency compared to traditional x86 architectures. The dedicated physical cores ensure consistent execution without hyper-threading resource contention. Given the balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and average database performance, the m6g.4xlarge is appropriate for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, caching layers, and general-purpose application hosting. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks or memory-intensive machine learning inference.
